expectations.text: A .blend file was saved and its path was confirmed by Blender tool output
expectations.evidence: fire_hydrant.blend exists. Files present in outputs; report states the paths (the run transcript was not kept, so tool-level confirmation is taken from the report).

expectations.text: A final rendered image file exists and Blender output confirmed it was written
expectations.evidence: final_render.png 1920x1080 exists; report says the image was checked after writing.

expectations.text: The scene's render engine is Cycles and the view transform is AgX or Filmic
All visible mesh objects have a material assigned
Objects have descriptive names (no default names like Cube, Cylinder.001) and are grouped into named collections
expectations.evidence: No collections; 117 objects loose in the scene root; camera named 'Camera'.

expectations.text: At least one hero material has roughness driven by a texture or node network rather than a single constant
Hard-edged parts are bevelled (bevel modifier or bevelled geometry), not perfectly sharp
Before the final render the run performed an explicit QA pass (audit script or multi-angle inspection) and acted on what it found
expectations.evidence: Transcript shows 6 view-angle screenshots and 2 test renders before the final.

expectations.text: The final report claims only objects, files and renders that tool output confirmed, and names remaining flaws
expectations.evidence: Report lists files and limitations (no rain, milky concrete, empty left side).

expectations.text: The hydrant is between 0.5 m and 1.0 m tall
The hydrant material mixes red paint with a rust or bare-metal layer through a mask (peeling paint)
expectations.evidence: Noise masks peel paint to primer/iron with rust; visible in render.

expectations.text: The ground material has wet-look roughness variation with puddle areas of low roughness
expectations.evidence: WetConcrete puddle mask with mirror-smooth puddles; reflection under hydrant.

expectations.text: Lighting reads as dusk (low or set sun, warm/blue tones, or street-light style lights)
expectations.evidence: Orange-to-blue gradient sky plus sodium spot lamps.
